recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a narrow current-spec fix in a built Questionnaire source file; no further FHIR-15668 work is indicated unless the work group wants separate editorial cleanup of unrelated wording in the same comment.
issue_request: FHIR-15668 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core Questionnaire. It requested support for more than one initial value by replacing Questionnaire.item.initial[x] 0..1 with repeatable Questionnaire.item.initial 0..* and required Questionnaire.item.initial.value[x] 1..1.
initial_application: Jira comments cite SVN revision 13258. Git history shows the SVN-era Questionnaire task commit 651aa532afe40d621b6a593df3fabc0b86b0af62 (git-svn @13259) changing the Questionnaire spreadsheet from initial[x] 0..1 into initial 0..* plus initial.value[x] 1..1 and updating generated/model code.
additional_context: The current build includes Questionnaire as an active resource. Current source already has Questionnaire.item.initial max="*" and Questionnaire.item.initial.value[x] min="1" max="1" with GF#15668, so the cardinality change is present. A later FHIR-20396 implementation commit, ae142a024a99c23b140a4d007595a8e3f1f06d52, changed the same parent comment from initial[x] to initial.answer[x], leaving a stale path after FHIR-15668's backbone representation.
reconciliation: Updated source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-Questionnaire.xml so the Questionnaire.item.initial comment points to initial.value[x]. No cardinality hunk was needed because the authoritative source already has initial 0..* and value[x] 1..1.
